NVIDIA fell 6% and Alphabet dropped 5% over the past month, amplifying index losses because market-cap weighting gives mega-caps outsized influence.

One Number: 337 Stocks Rose and the Index Still Fell

On Thursday, October 22, 2026, 337 S&P 500 stocks finished higher. Only 159 declined and 1 was unchanged across 497 tracked constituents. The index still closed lower. Most stocks rose and the benchmark fell, and that mismatch is a risk many retirement portfolios carry without the owners knowing it.

Nikada / E+ via Getty Images
What 337 Gainers Reveal About Your Index Fund

The S&P 500 is weighted by market value, so the biggest stocks have undue influence on the index's direction. Many investors use an index fund for broad market exposure, and those portfolios tilt heavily toward technology. One major S&P 500 index fund held 519 positions as of June 30, 2026, but Information Technology made up 38.0% of net assets and Communication Services added another 9.7%.

The concentration shows up clearly at the top. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) is valued at $5.09 trillion, Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) at $5.07 trillion, Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) at $3.97 trillion and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) at $3.89 trillion. When these giants slip together, hundreds of smaller gainers cannot pull the index up with them.

title: Bank of America revamps Meta stock price target once again
detail:
Bank of America revamps Meta stock price target once again
Hillary Remy, Aparajita Chatterjee
Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:07 AM EDT 5 min read
META
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Mark Zuckerberg had one message he wanted investors to hear on Oct. 21. "Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we're seeing velocity across the board," the Meta chief said in the company's earnings release.

Wall Street mostly bought it. At least 13 analysts raised their price targets after the report, yet the stock still fell sharply by midday on Oct. 22 as chipmakers and other big tech names slid alongside it. That gap between analyst enthusiasm and investor nerves is where the real story sits.

Bank of America raised its Meta price target to $845 from $810

Bank of America raised its price target on Meta Platforms to $845 from $810 and kept its buy rating. The new target implies an upside of roughly 21%, a strong vote of confidence in a company spending at a historic pace.

Also read: Meta Muse gives AMD and Intel investors a reason to cheer

The bank pointed to strong revenue growth driven by continued AI improvements in Meta's core advertising business. It also argued that Meta's base of about 3.6 billion users and 500 million enterprises gives it a running start in getting people to adopt new AI services. It added that growing visibility into AI monetization in 2027 should boost confidence in the returns on that spending.

Bank of America was far from alone.

JPMorgan lifted its target to $940 from $920, while UBS moved to $892 from $884, both keeping bullish ratings, with JPMorgan citing strong advertising, video growth and early momentum in Muse. Wells Fargo was a rare exception, trimming its target slightly even as it kept an overweight rating.

Not every firm moved in the same direction, but the overall tilt is bullish. MarketBeat puts the consensus at moderate buy, with an average target of $815.92. Bank of America's $845 sits above that midpoint, with room still left before the most aggressive calls.

Meta third-quarter beat behind the upgrade

The optimism starts with the top line. Meta's revenue rose 26% from a year earlier to $64.6 billion, beating expectations, and the company guided to $73 billion to $76 billion for the fourth quarter, according to Meta. Shares rose in after-hours trading as investors first reacted to the numbers.

Profit looked messier on paper. Meta reported earnings of $3.83 a share after taking a $9.89 billion legal charge tied to a settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health, according to Meta's earnings release. Excluding that charge, earnings came in at $7.40 a share.

The ad engine is doing the heavy lifting. Ad impressions rose 10% from a year earlier, while the average price per ad climbed 14%. Rising prices suggest advertisers are willing to pay more for the sharper targeting that AI tools are increasingly making possible.

title: Meet Wall Street's Newest Major Stock Split: It Has Soared 1,730% Since Its 2012 IPO, and There Is Plenty of Upside Left

Meet Wall Street's Newest Major Stock Split: It Has Soared 1,730% Since Its 2012 IPO, and There Is Plenty of Upside Left
Prosper Junior Bakiny, The Motley Fool
Sat, October 24, 2026 at 12:20 PM EDT 5 min read
META
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

A stock split is a corporate action in which a company increases the number of shares it has outstanding by dividing existing shares into multiple shares and proportionately decreasing its share price. Stock splits don't change a company's intrinsic value, but they can garner significant attention because they make each share more affordable, potentially increasing trading activity.

And the latest major corporation on Wall Street to announce a stock split is none other than Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META). The tech leader has beaten the broader equity market since its 2012 IPO, gaining a little over 1,700%. Yet, the stock still has outstanding long-term prospects.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Meta's strong third-quarter update

Meta Platforms announced its stock split alongside its third-quarter results. The split wasn't the best part of the company's update: Meta's financial performance during the period was pretty strong. Meta Platforms' revenue increased by 26% year over year to $64.6 billion.

True, the company's operating income dropped by 37% year over year to about $13 billion, but that was largely due to legal-related expenses. Meta recorded a $9.89 billion charge because of a recent legal settlement. Without that, the company's operating income would have increased by 11% year over year.

Besides, the legal settlement was worth the trouble. Meta Platforms agreed to pay up to $18 billion (with $12.7 billion guaranteed and $5.3 billion contingent on certain conditions) over 10 years to a bipartisan coalition of attorneys general representing dozens of U.S. states and territories in connection with lawsuits alleging that Meta's social media platforms have harmed consumers.

The amount is by no means catastrophic, especially considering the time frame. Returning to Meta's third-quarter results, the company posted earnings per share of $3.83, up 265% year over year, as the company's provision for income taxes dropped significantly. Meta also made progress elsewhere.

For instance, the company's daily active people across its websites and apps rose 3% year over year to 3.64 billion. Now turning to Meta's planned stock split, the company will create a new Class C non-voting common stock and issue one Class C share for each outstanding share.

What Happened?

Vistra (VST) closed down 9.81% at $140.83 on October 22, 2026, the session after Meta Platforms (META) reported third-quarter results. As CNBC reported, AI-linked stocks sold off broadly on worries about the soaring cost of data center expansion: Constellation Energy (CEG) closed down 5.74%, and Quanta Services (PWR) was down more than 8% in afternoon trading. Meta has signed 20-year nuclear contracts with Vistra, but management's own numbers suggest Vistra leans less on the data center boom than that selloff priced in.

Vistra Drawdowns (TIKR)
Vistra Already Marked Down the Data Center Queue

Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capital spending forecast to $135 billion and announced a new class of non-voting shares, which Reuters reported revived concern over its mounting capital commitments.

On Vistra's August 7 earnings call, President and CEO Jim Burke said ERCOT's data center queue has at times been described as over 400 GW, while Vistra expects roughly 12 to 15 GW by 2030. "So when you have numbers overstated by more than 20x, it causes problems for policymakers," Burke said. Of the 5% to 6% annual Texas load growth Vistra projects, he attributed about 3 points to oil and gas, residential, and small business demand and about 2 points to data centers. He gave a local example: eight data center projects were under consideration in one county near a Vistra nuclear plant, and he said "there is a reasonable chance there'll be no projects in that county."

If financing strain slows hyperscaler buildouts, speculative queue projects are likely to slip before signed contracts do. Most of the Meta deal rests on existing assets: according to Vistra's filings, 2,176 MW of the 2,609 MW comes from the operating Perry and Davis-Besse plants. Burke said equipment prices have, in some cases, "doubled, if not tripled," so buyers pay a premium for existing plants because they still cost less than new construction.

Vistra is not insulated, though. It has committed up to $1 billion to Helix Digital Infrastructure, a data center platform it joined with KKR, NVIDIA, and the Kuwait Investment Authority, with anything above $500 million tied to milestones.

What Happened?

Bloom Energy (BE) carried a forward P/E of around 78x on September 30. At the October 23 close of $193.30, it was around 40x. Two moves did the work in roughly equal measure: the stock fell 30.2%, and TIKR's next-twelve-months normalized EPS figure rose from around $3.50 to around $4.90.

AI power stocks sold off on October 22 as Meta Platforms' (META) results reignited AI spending concerns, and Bloom closed at $217.77 before its report. It fell another 11.24% on October 23 despite record quarterly revenue of $1.24 billion and a third 2026 guidance raise, while GE Vernova (GEV) slipped 1.50%. Coverage tied the drop to a $27 million operating cash outflow, which TIKR covered that day, plus valuation and broader AI sentiment.

Q3 Operating Income Topped All of 2025, Which Is Why Estimates Rose

Product revenue crossed $1 billion for the first time. Non-GAAP operating income reached $285.7 million, up more than 500%, while non-GAAP operating expenses grew 26% against revenue growth of 138.1%. Non-GAAP operating margin hit 23.1%, and Q3 operating income alone exceeded Bloom's total for all of 2025.

"That is the operating leverage embedded in our model now showing up in the results," CFO Simon Edwards said on the October 22 call. Non-GAAP product gross margin rose 120 basis points from Q2 to 38.4%, even as Bloom ramped new lines and expedited deliveries. Management raised non-GAAP operating income guidance to $960 million to $1.03 billion.

Bloom funded $231 million of year-to-date capex from operations and ended September with $2.5 billion of cash, though its convertible notes leave TIKR's LTM net debt at $299.89 million. At around 40x forward earnings, the stock now trades about level with GE Vernova's around 39x on TIKR's Competitors page. title: What the New Class C Share Structure Actually Means for Meta Platforms Stock Investors
detail:
What the New Class C Share Structure Actually Means for Meta Platforms Stock Investors
Aanchal Sugandh
Sat, October 24, 2026 at 7:16 AM EDT 5 min read
META
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Meta Platforms (META) is introducing non-voting Class C shares to widen its options for raising capital, rewarding employees, and financing acquisitions without weakening CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control. On Wednesday, Oct. 21, the board approved the charter amendment alongside its Q3 results, with a revised certificate of incorporation scheduled to take effect on Tuesday, Jan. 19, 2027.

Under the new arrangement, existing shareholders will receive one Class C share for every outstanding Class A or Class B share they own. Meta expects its Class A share price to reflect a two-for-one stock split following the distribution, while the board will determine the record date and payment date for shareholders.

Beyond giving Meta greater financial flexibility, the arrangement also supports Zuckerberg's continued leadership amid concerns over California's proposed wealth tax, Proposition 40.

Under a Founder Alignment Agreement, he would receive non-voting Class C shares that could provide liquidity to cover a potential multibillion-dollar tax liability, in exchange for committing to remain a California resident or live wherever Meta maintains its headquarters for eight years, subject to limited exceptions.

The initial distribution resembles a stock split, but the broader framework has longer-term implications. By creating another avenue for capital raising, employee compensation, and strategic acquisitions, Meta would be able to finance its expansion with greater flexibility while preserving its existing governance structure.

About Meta Stock

Meta Platforms has evolved well beyond its social media beginnings. Based in Menlo Park, California, the company connects users through Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, Threads, and Meta AI. Its Reality Labs division extends that reach into Quest headsets, artificial intelligence (AI) glasses, and related technologies, alongside virtual and augmented reality.

That breadth has helped Meta become one of the technology sector's biggest players, with a market cap of about $1.8 trillion. Its share-price performance, however, has been far less convincing. META stock has fallen 11.5% over the past 52 weeks and declined 1.7% year-to-date (YTD). The recent slide has been sharper, with shares dropping 11.9% over the past month.
